summary: Delta 534d7ff..HEAD: all five round-1 blocking findings are verified fixed (models-record locked state writer, roles/tiers.json from authored frontmatter, symlinked-.factory refusal, bounded no-follow config read, truthful FR-003 adapter prose; test_models 12/12 and tier-parity green; the design-to-code permissions failure is pre-existing and excluded). Three blocking findings remain. SEC-1 is a new high command-injection defect introduced by the fix itself: SKILL.md:47 interpolates repository-controlled model values into a single-quoted shell command; judge reproduction executed a $(...) substitution from a project model value. SPEC-1 and SPEC-2 are confirmed-scope non-delivery, not mere advisory re-reports: plan.md:118 (user-confirmed fix-round scope, Q13 relay, commit 75d09e6) declares control-character refusal + table sanitize, publish-race refusal with temp cleanup, and retryable no-artifact init; the delta ships none of the three (no sanitize/escape anywhere in the CLI, os.replace still overwrites, config.json published before README with mid-loop OSErrors uncaught), and engineering.md's Confirmed test scope rule rates missing coverage of confirmed scope as a HIGH finding that blocks. The medium code-level facets of those clusters (TOCTOU overwrite, half-complete init, control-sequence interpolation) merge into the blocking entries as same-defect sources; the round-1 advisory severity would have kept them advisory absent the confirmed scope. Two low advisories (init README sentence, FR-003 spec text) go to the user at approver. The per-project-models feature itself is not invalidated: resolution, precedence, state recording and the tier map work and are tested; every blocking item lives in the models-record transport (SKILL.md/cli.py) and the init publish loop (models.py), fixable in one focused round.

confirmed_blocking.summary: Preflight instruction interpolates repository-controlled model values into a single-quoted shell command, permitting command execution (ENG-25; violates plan.md's 'values are passed as model IDs only, never executed')
confirmed_blocking.evidence: New in this delta (commit 482a27b): SKILL.md:47 instructs `SHELL: python3 <F>/bin/factory models-record '<JSON block>'` with the block built from `factory models --json` output. _read_models accepts any string (models.py:43-51 checks only isinstance str), and json.dumps does not escape apostrophes, so a project model like `x'$(touch /tmp/MARKER)'` in .factory/config.json closes the shell quote, executes command substitution with the invoking user's permissions, and reopens it. Judge reproduction: resolver passed the payload verbatim (`"model": "x'$(touch /tmp/sec1repro/MARKER)'"`, source project) and running the exact SKILL.md command form under /bin/sh created the MARKER file while the reassembled JSON argument stayed valid. The injection fires in every preflight, before the CLI validates anything, and runs with the orchestrating user's permissions on a malicious checkout.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Do not interpolate model values into shell syntax. Resolve the block inside the CLI (models-record takes only the harness/tier selection and re-reads the resolver output itself), or define a non-shell safe transport (argv array or stdin) and document it in SKILL.md and the adapters; add an adversarial apostrophe/command-substitution regression test that proves no model value can escape the transport.

confirmed_blocking.summary: User-confirmed fix-round scope 'control-character model values refused (resolve + table sanitize)' (plan.md:118) shipped no code and no test: values are still accepted unfiltered and interpolated raw into the terminal table and README (SPEC-1 missing declared coverage per engineering.md Confirmed test scope; ENG-4/ENG-18; ENG-25 code facet)
confirmed_blocking.evidence: plan.md:118, confirmed by the user (relay Q13, commit 75d09e6) as fix-round-1 seam scope, declares 'control-character model values refused (resolve + table sanitize)'. The delta implements none of it: _read_models (models.py:43-51) validates only object shape, known harness, known tier and string type; report() interpolates values raw into the human-readable table (models.py:91 f"{harness}  {tier}  {value}  {source}"); init embeds the same raw table in config.README.md (models.py:105-111); grep for sanitize/escape/shlex across models.py, commands.py and cli.py returns nothing; test_models.py adds no such test. engineering.md: 'Missing coverage or absent/stale scope acceptance blocks implementation with a HIGH finding'; no fresh confirmation reduced the scope. Code facet: a project value containing an escaped OSC 52 sequence reaches the terminal verbatim.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Reject model values containing C0/C1 control characters in _read_models, sanitize them in report()/README output, and add the declared failure-path test; or obtain fresh protected confirmation through the orchestrator removing this failure path from the declared scope.

confirmed_blocking.summary: User-confirmed fix-round scope 'init publish race: existing destination at publish -> refusal with temp cleanup; init publish failure leaves no artifacts (retryable)' (plan.md:118) shipped no code and no test: the final publish is still an overwriting os.replace and config.json is published before config.README.md with mid-loop failures surfacing as raw tracebacks (SPEC-2 missing declared coverage per engineering.md Confirmed test scope; ENG-4/ENG-18; ENG-26/ENG-17 code facets: TOCTOU clobber and unrecoverable half-complete init)
confirmed_blocking.evidence: init checks config.exists() or config.is_symlink() (models.py:98), then the new dirfd loop creates the temp with O_EXCL (models.py:131-133) but publishes with os.replace(name, filename, src_dir_fd=dirfd, dst_dir_fd=dirfd) (models.py:137), which unconditionally overwrites a config.json created in the race window, silently losing the other writer's bytes - the declared refusal-with-temp-cleanup path does not exist (only the finally-unlink temp cleanup does, models.py:139-143). The loop publishes ("config.json", ...) before ("config.README.md", ...) (models.py:121-126) and only the dirfd os.open converts OSError to ModelConfigError (models.py:117-119), so a README-stage failure propagates as an uncaught traceback (cli.py:445-454 catches ModelConfigError/StateError/CLIError only) and leaves a half-complete bootstrap that FR-013 requires whole, with retries refused by the exists() check at models.py:98 - the declared no-artifact retryable path does not exist. No test covers either failure path; no fresh confirmation reduced the declared scope.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Publish with no-replace semantics (linkat/renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) equivalent or an exclusive-creation protocol) refusing with cleanup when a destination appears, stage both outputs so a mid-init failure leaves nothing recoverable (or make config.README.md precede config.json as the commit point), convert loop failures to ModelConfigError diagnostics, and add the two declared failure-path tests; or obtain fresh protected confirmation reducing the scope.

advisory.summary: Init-seeded config.README.md still states 'An empty string inherits the session model.', contradicting the FR-003 accuracy fix shipped in the same round (ENG-7 prose accuracy)
advisory.fix: Update the init README sentence to match the adapter disclosure: an empty value inherits the session model only when the installed agent has no configured model; omission does not clear a pinned model.

advisory.summary: FR-003's MUST text ('inherit the session's model') is left unamended while the accepted resolution ships a stop-and-disclose rule for model-pinned installed agents, leaving spec and shipped guidance divergent
advisory.fix: Record the accepted limitation in spec.md FR-003 (or a clarification) so the MUST text and the shipped stop-and-disclose rule agree; the user can accept the divergence at approver instead.
